title: eIM: GPU-Accelerated Efficient Influence Maximization in Large-Scale Social Networks
problem: Influence maximization (IM) in large networks is NP-hard. State-of-the-art GPU IMM (Influence Maximization via Martingales) algorithm incurs significant memory overhead from storing random reverse reachable (RRR) sets, limiting scalability.
motivation: Social network analysis and information propagation modeling require efficient IM. GPU IMM implementations show promise but memory footprint limits applicability to largest networks.
method: eIM reduces the memory overhead of influence maximization on GPU by storing reverse reachable (RRR) sets—the random path samples used to estimate influence spread—more efficiently. The approach cuts memory requirements for the network data and RRR sets by 54% while maintaining accuracy compared to baseline GPU implementations. This frees up GPU memory, allowing the algorithm to handle much larger networks.
key_novelty: eIM's core insight is that reverse reachable sets can be stored more efficiently on GPU, reducing memory requirements by 54% while achieving 1-3 order-of-magnitude speedups in influence maximization compared to prior GPU implementations.
contributions: 1-3 orders of magnitude speedups over GPU implementations
